label: def:transfer-matrix-operator
title: Transfer Matrix Operator for Nuclear Braid Interactions
html:
Every particle interaction in the Descartes universe encodes as a transfer matrix T_{K_1, K_2}(q) \in \mathrm{M}_2(\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}]) acting on the Gröbner–Shirshov ideal of the Iwahori–Hecke algebra, with entries that are polynomials in q.

Definition. Let K_1, K_2 be two building block knots (building blocks) meeting at a crossing in a braid word \beta \in B_n. The transfer matrix of the crossing is:

  T_{K_1, K_2}(q)
  = 
  \begin{pmatrix}
    c(q - q^{-1}) + d & c \\
    c & d
  \end{pmatrix}

where the crossing coefficients (c, d) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}]^2 are determined by the knot types:

  c_{K_1, K_2}
  = 
  \frac{J_{K_1}(q) \cdot J_{K_2}(q)}{J_{K_1 \# K_2}(q)},
  \qquad
  d_{K_1, K_2}
  = 
  -c \cdot \frac{q  s}{1 + J_{K_1}(q) \cdot J_{K_2}(q)}

where J_K(q) is the Jones polynomial of knot K and s = q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2} is the Skein amplitude.

For the three nuclear crossing types (quarks as Borromean unknot components), this specializes to:

Crossing K_1 K_2 c d Hecke element
\mathfrak{p}-\mathfrak{p} u u 1 0 \sigma
\mathfrak{n}-\mathfrak{n} d d 1 -(q - q^{-1}) \sigma^{-1}
mixed u d 1 -\frac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) \frac{1}{2}(\sigma + \sigma^{-1})
